item.description: Don’t miss a free conversation with two outstanding social justice authors! Register at tinyurl.com/OBOMMcGhee Economist Heather McGhee will be talking with legendary civil rights attorney Michelle Alexander about McGhee’s landmark bestseller, “The Sum of Us: What Racism Costs All of Us and How We Can Prosper Together.” Thanks to the generosity of our co-sponsor, Partners for Health Foundation, the first 100 guests to enter the event will receive a free copy of the book. “[‘The Sum of Us’ is] stunning, sobering…hopeful…Abandoning the zero-sum thinking at the heart of U.S. history — which pits racial groups against one another, as if one can win only if others lose — will unlock the benefits of social cooperation. The result can be a ‘solidarity dividend’ that easily outweighs the meager rations of racist division and purely psychic wages.”—The Washington Post. Doors open at 6:30 p.m. The discussion will be followed by an audience Q&A and book sales and signing with Watchung Bookselle

item.title: Close Encounters of the 34th Avenue Kind: A Documentary Screening & Conversation — Thu Oct 15, 6:30 PM — Montclair State University School of Communication & Media
item.description: Join us at Montclair State University for a special screening of Close Encounters of the 34th Avenue Kind, an exciting documentary exploring how streets, transportation, and public space shape our daily lives and communities. It IS inspiring, and we’re happy to have it kick off Bloomfield Avenue is a Commons initiative. Bloomfield Avenue Is a Commons reimagines the Avenue as shared civic infrastructure that connects not only cities & towns, urban & suburban, but people. Using public discourse, in-person events, storytelling, art, and analysis, we explore how streets can function as places for connection and democratic life. The documentary features the work and perspective of Clarence Eckerson Jr., founder of Streetfilms and one of the world’s most influential storytellers on transportation, cities, and public space. item.description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.
⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.
🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).
**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one
